claude.sample_unit: clinicians completing assessment of 50 real-world spirometry records

links.outcome: Preferred diagnosis agreement with expert reference, clinicians with versus without AI decision support
links.effect: AI support improved preferred diagnosis performance in all cases (mean difference 9.0; 95% CI 4.5 to 13.3%; P=0.001) and COPD cases (15.9; 95% CI 9.0 to 22.7%; P<0.001).
links.quote: Compared with the control group, the addition of AI decision support software led to improvements in preferred diagnosis prediction performance in all cases (mean difference, 9.0; 95% CI, 4.5 to 13.3%; P=0.001) and in COPD cases (15.9; 95% CI, 9.0 to 22.7%; P<0.001).

links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic performance with AI in intended workflow versus without AI
links.effect: AI adjunct improved clinician preferred diagnosis performance (mean difference 9.0%; COPD 15.9%); differential diagnosis and technical quality assessment also improved, not pattern interpretation or confidence.
links.quote: Differential diagnosis prediction and technical quality assessment performance also improved with intervention, but not pattern interpretation or clinician confidence levels.

screen.practice: AI decision support for clinician spirometry interpretation (with vs without)
screen.reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating the impact of AI decision support software on primary care clinicians interpreting spirometry records versus unassisted clinician interpretation.
